People's Majlis Committee Minutes

13th meeting of the Environment and Climate Change Committee

21 October 2026

Venue: People's Majlis G (Committee Room 8)

Start time: 11:10

{Presiding: the Committee Chair, Member for South Maafannu constituency Abdulla Rifau}

Chair speaking:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم. Welcome to the 13th meeting of the People's Majlis Environment and Climate Change Committee. The meeting is being held in Committee Room 8. Today's date is 21 October 2026, Wednesday. The time is 11:10. Today's agenda is to review the work before the Committee. Accordingly: the resolution submitted to ascertain the views of Members of the People's Majlis on the high cost that small and medium businesses operating in regions other than Malé have to pay for the electricity and water services they use, whose deadline expired on 4 November 2025. The assessment prepared on permitting beverage bottles packaged in plastic smaller than five hundred ml in the Maldives. The letter sent by Project Thimaaveshi and several other associations sharing concerns about the damage from reducing the protected area of Eidhigali and Koattey for the work of a project planned to widen the Link Road in Hithadhoo, Addu City. The letter sent sharing concerns about the land reclamation work in the Moolekede Fishimathi area of Addu. The matter submitted regarding relocating the B. Goidhoo engine [unclear] to another area. The letter sent by Maldives Resilient Reefs requesting a meeting to share with the Committee the findings of the study it has carried out. The matter submitted requesting the relevant offices to clarify a date by which water, sewerage and electricity services can be provided to the one hundred housing units built in M. Kolhufushi, as the work needed to provide those services has not started. When clarified administratively through the council president, information was received that the water and sewerage work is proceeding by FENAKA and that the electricity service work is not proceeding by STELCO.

Chair speaking:
So, the first matter now is the resolution submitted by Rifau concerning electricity and water for small and medium businesses operating in regions other than Malé, whose

deadline has now expired on 4 November 2025. So we will have to amend this deadline again. So I open the floor for your views on this. Member for West Maafannu constituency Mohamed Musthafa.

Member for West Maafannu constituency Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim speaking:
It seems that work has been done in the Committee and, with the information requested from the relevant parties also received, we can carry this work through and complete it before 30 November. So I propose that the deadline be set as 30 November. Thank you.

Chair speaking:
Member for Mathiveri constituency Hassan Zareer.

Member for Mathiveri constituency Hassan Zareer speaking:
On this matter, I take the opportunity to say that I second the deadline just proposed by the honourable Member.

Chair speaking:
Thank you. Yes! Now there is a proposal on the first matter and it has been seconded. So I will put it to a vote accordingly. Those in favour please raise your hands. (Voting) Thank you. At this time ten members are present in the Committee. Of the ten members, nine voted and the vote has been concluded unanimously. Yes! At this point I will announce the members present in the Committee at this time today. Yes! I apologise, I announced that incorrectly just now. At this time eight members are present in the Committee. Seven members are in a position to vote. With the votes of seven members this proposal has been passed unanimously. Present in the Committee at this time are Member for South Maafannu constituency Abdulla Rifau

(myself), Member for Central Hulhumalé constituency Abdulla Shazeem, Member for West Maafannu constituency Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim, Member for Mathiveri constituency Hassan Zareer, Member for Hithaadhoo constituency Mohamed Siruhaan, Member for Gemanafushi constituency Asadhulla Shihab, Member for Keyodhoo constituency Mohamed Niushad, Member for North Hithadhoo constituency Abdulla Sodig. Next I will move to today's second matter. The second matter is the assessment prepared on permitting beverage bottles packaged in plastic smaller than five hundred ml in the Maldives. So, actually, on this matter this Committee has also carried out studies, and we have obtained in writing from the Economic Ministry and also the Environment Ministry their views on this, and have been monitoring how they are proceeding with that work. So, now, going by the latest decree issued by the President, we believe we have now obtained the desired solution on this matter. I now open the Committee for further views on this. Member for West Maafannu constituency Mohamed Musthafa.

Member for West Maafannu constituency Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim speaking:
I think this matter can now be closed if the question is answered in this new way. Under the President's decree, all sizes above 250 ml are now, above 250 ml is now permitted. Previously that was 500 ml. Now it has changed to 250 ml. I believe that was the main concern raised. So that concern has now been resolved. The government has arranged that. So I consider that this matter can be closed at this point by answering in that way. So I propose that, referring to the President's decree, the party be informed that the decree has now been decided this way.

Chair speaking:
Member for Gemanafushi constituency Asadhulla.

Member for Gemanafushi constituency Asadhulla Shihab speaking:
I second the proposal made by Member for West Maafannu constituency Musthafa Ibrahim.

Chair speaking:
Yes! Thank you. Now there is a proposal on this matter and it has been seconded. Therefore, I will put this proposal to a vote. Those in favour, hands up. (Voting) Yes! Thank you. At this time 7 honourable members are present for the vote. Among them 6 members are in a position to vote. With the votes of 6 members this proposal has been carried unanimously. Therefore, the matter that came to this Committee regarding permitting beverage bottles packaged in plastic smaller than 500 ml in the Maldives will be filed. And in connection with that matter, the Committee will respond in writing to the party that submitted it. Next is the letter sent by Project Thimaaveshi and other associations sharing concerns about the damage that would result from reducing the protected area in Eidhigali and Koattey for the work of a project planned to widen the Link Road in Hithadhoo, Addu City. (After a short while) The honourable Member for Vilifushi constituency Hassan Waheed has joined us in the Committee. (After a short while) Yes! Thank you. Member for West Maafannu constituency Mohamed Musthafa.

Member for West Maafannu constituency Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim speaking:
I have just a small request, you know. The matter has been stated very clearly. And the letter sent by the ministry in relation to it is also very clear. It is being noted that the two sides are saying two different things. So I would just request that, since our honourable Member for North Hithadhoo constituency Sodig is now sitting on the Environment Committee, he say something on this. As it is a very important matter. Because I do not know about that area and how things have turned out.

Chair speaking:
Member for North Hithadhoo constituency Abdulla Sodig.

Member for North Hithadhoo constituency Abdulla Sodig speaking:
Thank you, Chair. There are important points to note in the matter submitted. The matter highlighted is that part of a protected area in Hithadhoo, that is, part of the Addu Nature Park area, was added to the Link Road. When the Link Road was being built in 2022, looking at implementing the Link Road project, even as it was roughly designed, the road ran onto some plots that had been allocated there. Because of that, after consultation with the EPA and the Environment Ministry, about 10 feet was permitted from the buffer zone of the protected area. That is in the very same area as it is now. However, slightly to the side. The roughly 10 feet added was connected to a road built right next to it that already exists. There is a road called "Senda". That is a wide road. Buses also travel on that road now. Now the project was changed again in 2024, and in 2025 the project was extended to connect the road to another road. Because of that, 2 more hectares had to be reclaimed. That reclamation was needed because of an issue some people in that area kept complaining about: the water becoming salty. Everyone also knows the settlement there; that area is close to the wetland and close to the sea. It is an area that is always salty. So piped water is also supplied there. The groundwater there is reasonably good to some extent. However, during the road building and the drainage system works that took place from 2022, two pump stations were built in that area to house the pumps required. When those two pump stations were built, a great deal of water was pumped out, to build their tanks. Because of pumping water over many days, the water around this area became much saltier. So the water becoming salty is actually the people's problem. Now the water is not improving much because of the reclaimed sand. So reclamation went ahead from this area, and as reclamation proceeded, the EIA also states that the mangroves there, it is an area with a great many kandoo trees. All the types mentioned here, dhingaa, madi, crabs, among the crabs

in particular it is an area where these very large crabs live, called Lanka crab, also called mud crab. Scylla serrata, something very rare in the Maldives too. That type of crab has been found in Addu only in that area. So a large area of this place is being reclaimed. Now, as reclamation reached the mangroves, that project too has been stopped. That is how things currently stand. However, in a project that reclaimed a very large area, the EIA requires that the mangroves there be removed and planted on the other side, on the other side of the same land, on the eastern side. Mangroves are not something that can be made by planting them that way. So I think discussions on how to do that are also taking place between the two ministries. However, the project is stopped. It is not moving forward. That is how it stands. However, this does not solve the people's problem. The people's problem is the water becoming salty. Even before, that area, being close to the wetland and the sea, was salty. So it became saltier, as I said, because of pumping water to build two pump stations. Not really because of the wetland being there. And when the wetland goes, a very large mangrove area of the nature park is lost. Environmentally, many species, what the people of that area call madi live there, madi breed and there are lots of small madi. You will see this place; in the videos made, the videos the young people made, you can see that even when they went there, there were small madi and such nearby. And there is even a special name: the deep hole there is called "Madivada" by the people of that area. An area named especially for the madi. It is an area where the people of that area still catch and eat crabs. So if that area disappears, the populations of many living things will be lost. Besides crabs, dhingaa and many things of that kind will be lost. Now, however, two hectares, about two hectares out of 2.5, have been reclaimed. And yet it is a problem that does not get solved. It does not solve the people's problem. That is the water, the water salinity problem. The water salinity is now improving to some extent compared to before, the water is recovering. However, it will not be solved completely. And since that area is a wetland, there will always be a smell anyway. That smell will not go away. Those kinds of things are the people's complaints. Therefore,

had the place been changed in a better way than that, with the road laid as it was before, exactly as planned, and since that area is environmentally important and is a protected nature park area, had it been cleaned up and kept in a way that people could make use of it, it could have been managed better than before. However, now the place is not finished at all. The project has ended at this point. That is the update. That is from what I can see and from the information I have received. And I cannot accept, I never at any time accept that this is something we really had to do in order to build the road. And I also discussed it at great length with the council. The council also does not agree with it. And when the EIA was done, it also came up with me when meeting members of the association I belong to. I did not accept the EIA then, and I still cannot accept that the project must proceed the way it has now been implemented. Thank you.

Chair speaking:
So, how about writing again to the two ministries to get the latest update on this matter? Then we will know where it stands now, and can proceed on the matter. So let us proceed that way.

Member for West Maafannu constituency Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim speaking:
I think the reply to the letter has been received. Actually, even if we get one, I think this kind of reply is probably what will come again. Perhaps another way should be found. That is, in fact the ministry also says that this project is noted more as a project connected to the people's health and general living than as a project carried out on the basis of a development vision; that 68% of the people support this project; that, because of the project, the water lens in that area which has now deteriorated is improving; that when this is completed it will also pave the way for waste management; that, taking into account the environmental concerns, this ministry gives priority to carrying out the work in line with the recommendations in the report, that is, in line with the EIA report;

and protecting the mangrove area, and then, the project having stopped when it reached that point, right, because it would be damaged, protecting it even by moving it to another area; and that work is under way to bring protection, using natural methods to protect the beaches, if that is included in the project. And it also assures that all necessary measures will be taken fully to reduce the adverse impacts on the environment from the important work being carried out to resolve the difficulties faced by the people. Now, if we were to ask, what we would really need to ask is what is being done at this time to reduce the adverse impacts on the environment, or how things have come to this point now. I think that is what we need to ask. We could actually send that to clarify it. That could perhaps be done. Otherwise, I will have to go and look at the area myself with the help of the honourable Member for North Hithadhoo constituency. I see that this letter right here notes, right, that measures are being taken. So, what measures are those, I think, having looked; and why? I propose that those two questions actually be sent to get the answers.

Chair speaking:
Honourable Member for Vilifushi constituency Hassan Waheed. Member for West Maafannu constituency Mohamed Musthafa.

Member for West Maafannu constituency Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim speaking:
I will restate my proposal in a slightly clearer way. The thing is, this letter says it assures that the measures will be taken fully. So, within that assurance, what is now, what kind of measures are being taken for that protection? And we just learned from the honourable Member, the honourable Member for North Hithadhoo constituency, that the project is currently stopped. So, to carry that project forward, now

what work has been done and what is the plan, let us send again to clarify that information.

Chair speaking:
Honourable Member for Vilifushi constituency Hassan Waheed.

Member for Vilifushi constituency Hassan Waheed speaking:
Yes! Thank you, Chair. I can second the proposal made by the honourable Member for West Maafannu constituency Mohamed Musthafa. I too believe that clarifying what further measures they are taking to protect that environment is important for us as well. Yes! And then the project, what is the project's plan now. I say this because I can support clarifying both of these things. I second that proposal. Thank you.

Chair speaking:
Now there is a proposal on this matter, submitted and seconded. Therefore, I ask you to vote as you see fit on this proposal. (Voting) Thank you. The proposal just made has passed with the unanimous votes of the five members in a position to vote, out of the six members present at this time. Therefore, I ask the secretariat desk to take this forward. Next is Addu Meedhoo; Member for North Hithadhoo constituency Abdulla Sodig.

Member for North Hithadhoo constituency Abdulla Sodig speaking:
Yes! This matter actually came to this Committee, as I understand it, urging that this project not proceed this way. However, the project has gone ahead anyway. When the project work was carried out, not a single thing stated in the EIA was done. In fact, for protection, for environmental protection,

nothing at all was done. It was reclaimed by dumping the sand that had been taken and stockpiled when Hithadhoo land was reclaimed. When the sand ran out, it has now been stopped. And to date not a single kandoo tree there, not a single mangrove tree has been protected there. The project is not in a state to proceed further either. The place is very badly destroyed. That is something I want to note. And in any case, if something is done now, if that road is built, the road is being connected to a road that is narrower than before; the Link Road is connected to a one-lane road. It is a very narrow road even for running buses. So in reality this does not solve the problem that arose of the water in that area deteriorating, the water becoming salty. It still does not solve it. Even before this project the water in that area was not that good. It is an area affected by salinity. An area where the water is deteriorated, with water deterioration too. The problem that arose was caused by pumping. The project's consultant engineers at the time, of the road building project, have said that this would gradually resolve even if this project did not go ahead this way. So, for the record, I note that in reality what was done here was something that destroyed the environment. Actually, now is not a time when the things requested in the matter submitted can be done. Now is not an appropriate time either. That project has gone ahead that way. Reclamation of that place is finished. The ministry has not even checked for us whether what the EIA said is being followed. So in this, I think, even now, since you are writing the letter again to get very good information, finding out what was done within this project to protect the environment and what work can be done to complete the project again is important. Yes! Thank you.

Chair speaking:
Yes! Thank you. As it is now time for the vote, we will conclude today's Committee at this point. And I will call another Committee meeting again next week. Thank you.
